Users who are still shaping a business can work on it here before they have a store. None of these tools needs one.
- Naming: generate-business-names suggests business names from a short description of what the user sells, who it is for, or the feeling they want.
- Domains: generate-domain-names checks whether a name or domain idea is available and what it costs to register, and suggests available alternatives.
When the user settles on a name, offer to check domains for it.
Never present a domain as available unless generate-domain-names checked it; a domain you suggest yourself may already be taken.
Follow the user's lead rather than walking them through every step.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.

- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.

1. Prefer a built-in tool when it matches the request.
2. Otherwise, start at graphql_schema with operation 'query' to discover the exact query field rather than guessing.

1. graphql_schema with operation 'query': list the top-level query names or search them, then inspect the exact field_name to learn its arguments and return type.
2. graphql_schema with operation 'schema' and type_name: inspect each named argument and return type needed to select fields or construct variables. Follow named nested input types with further calls.
3. Construct the query, then call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before execution. Do NOT skip validation.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.
# brief

- `brief.md` - the participant brief (max. 4 pages)
- `api.md` - the HTTP API reference
- `submission.md` - what to submit on Sunday, and how the pitch works
# Supplier scorecard - method

Each row (`sc:<supplier>@<quarter>`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to
the supplier, so both sides know it.

- **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the
  requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date.
  Partial deliveries count as separate lines.
- **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN).
- **open_8d_overdue**: supplier-caused complaints older than 60 days without a closed 8D report at quarter end.
- **score** = 0.5 x otd_pct + 0.5 x quality points - 5 x open_8d_overdue, with quality points =
  100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000).
- **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.

right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.
# brief

- `brief.md` - the participant brief (max. 4 pages)
- `api.md` - the HTTP API reference
- `submission.md` - what to submit on Sunday, and how the pitch works
# Supplier scorecard - method

Each row (`sc:<supplier>@<quarter>`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to
the supplier, so both sides know it.

- **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the
  requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date.
  Partial deliveries count as separate lines.
- **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN).
- **open_8d_overdue**: supplier-caused complaints older than 60 days without a closed 8D report at quarter end.
- **score** = 0.5 x otd_pct + 0.5 x quality points - 5 x open_8d_overdue, with quality points =
  100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000).
- **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.

"""SimplifyAgent: slim reciprocal agent. Anchor, steady matched concessions, RFQ round-robin.

Every choice among candidate sheets is priced with cost.total_cost, over the five parts of C:
1. price: anchor 0.80 x theirs, steady concessions matched to theirs;
2. uncovered need: contract length and volume are the options with the lowest C (never leave need uncovered);
3. payment, freight, lead time: each negotiable lever takes its lowest-C option, unless the supplier pinned it;
4. quality and other: ppm commitment likewise, plus a second sheet with an index clause for a higher price;
5. the supplier's health (strategic / bottleneck goals with a relationship cost): C charges for leaving the supplier below a
   sustainable margin, but the buyer cannot estimate its full cost (should-cost exists for about half the parts and can exceed
   the price), so cost.total_cost sees 0 and the mock does not price it. Safer rule there, UNTESTED against the real penalty:
   anchor 0.90 and only levers that cost the supplier nothing (contract length, volume); payment, freight, lead time and
   quality stay at the supplier's own terms.

Closing, must-have and pin helpers are shared with reciprocal.py."""

import math

from ..cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, complete_offer, total_cost
from ..docs import standard_terms
from ..guard import satisfy_must_haves
from ..play import closing_move, latest, moves_left
from .reciprocal import (
    ANCHOR,
    ANCHOR_FLOOR,
    FRAC0,
    FRAC_MAX,
    FRAC_STEP,
    KEEP,
    MATCH,
    MIN_STEP,
    MOVING_MIN,
    _c_alt,
    _live,
    _mine,
    _pinned,
    _sup,
    _tick,
    _valid,
    case_c_open,
    closing_accept,
)

EASED_ANCHOR = 0.90
STALL = 0.01  # the supplier's best C fell by less than this (x C) across its last two replies: it has stalled
GAP = 0.05  # then our offer rises until it is at most this far (x their C) below theirs
FREE_LEVERS = ("contract_months", "volume_per_year")  # cost the supplier nothing in cash
LEVERS = ("contract_months", "volume_per_year", "payment_days", "incoterm", "lead_time_days", "ppm_commitment")


def _health_at_stake(case):
    """C charges for the supplier's margin (strategic / bottleneck goal with a price per margin point)."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    return b.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS and bool(b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"))


class SimplifyAgent:
    _c_open = math.inf  # set per decision; our offer never costs more than the closing rule would accept

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        if not _live(threads):  # nothing to answer
            return {"supplier_id": next(iter(threads), None), "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        if accept := closing_accept(case, threads):
            return accept
        live = [s for s in _live(threads) if moves_left(case, threads[s]) >= 1]
        open_ = [s for s in live if latest(threads[s]).get("status") not in ("final_offer", "agreed")]
        if not open_:
            return closing_move(case, threads)

        def key(s):  # keep every thread moving: fewest messages first, then the cheapest
            ev = threads[s]
            c = min((c for c, _ in _valid(case, ev, standard_terms(ev), math.inf, musts=False)), default=math.inf)
            return len(_mine(ev)), c

        sid = min(open_, key=key)
        # cap: the opening and the best standing sheet of any other open thread
        others = [c for s in open_ if s != sid for c, _ in _valid(case, threads[s], standard_terms(threads[s]), math.inf)]
        self._c_open = min([case_c_open(case, threads), *others])
        events = threads[sid]
        std = standard_terms(events)
        valid = _valid(case, events, std, math.inf) or _valid(case, events, std, math.inf, musts=False)  # a must-have breach is fixed in our sheet
        if not valid:  # no priced sheet to answer: ask for one, give up after 3 asks
            if len(_mine(events)) >= 3:
                return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"subject": case.get("title", "Our enquiry"), "body": "Could you please send us your quote?"}}
        _, best = min(valid, key=lambda v: v[0])
        sheets = self._sheets(case, events, std, best["terms"])
        if not sheets:  # nothing new left to offer: close on the best sheet, or give up
            return closing_move(case, threads)
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case.get("title", "Our proposal"),
                "body": "Thank you for your offer. We have moved on our side; please see our updated terms.",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
            },
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _their_move(events):
        """How far the supplier's best price fell in its last message (0 if it did not)."""
        ps = [min(s["terms"]["unit_price"] for s in m["term_sheets"] if s["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None)
              for m in _sup(events) if any(s["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None for s in m["term_sheets"])]
        return max(0.0, ps[-2] - ps[-1]) if len(ps) >= 2 else 0.0

    @staticmethod
    def _stalled(case, events, std):
        """We have opened and the supplier's best C fell by < STALL across its last two replies (3+ priced messages)."""
        cs = [min(total_cost(case, t["terms"], std) for t in m["term_sheets"] if t["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None)
              for m in _sup(events) if any(t["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None for t in m["term_sheets"])]
        return bool(_mine(events)) and len(cs) >= 3 and cs[-3] - cs[-1] < STALL * cs[-3]

    def _price(self, case, events, p):
        mine = [m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"] for m in _mine(events) if m.get("term_sheets") and m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"].get("unit_price")]
        if not mine:
            cur = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price") or p
            return max(ANCHOR_FLOOR * p, min((EASED_ANCHOR if _health_at_stake(case) else ANCHOR) * p, cur))  # anchor; never pay more than now unless forced
        frac = min(FRAC_MAX, FRAC0 + FRAC_STEP * len(mine))
        move = self._their_move(events)
        step = max(frac * (p - mine[-1]), MIN_STEP * p, _tick(p))
        if move > 0:  # they moved: answer in step, not beyond (a supplier that holds still gets the full step)
            step = max(MOVING_MIN * p, _tick(p), min(step, MATCH * move))
        top = p if moves_left(case, events) <= 2 else p * (1 - KEEP)
        return max(mine[-1], min(top, mine[-1] + step))

    def _sheets(self, case, events, std, theirs):
        p, pins = theirs["unit_price"], _pinned(events)
        base = {k: v for k, v in {**{f: std[f] for f in case["negotiable"] if f in std}, **theirs}.items() if v is not None}
        opts = case.get("term_options") or {}
        c_alt = _c_alt(case)
        sent = [m["term_sheets"] for m in _mine(events) if m.get("term_sheets")]
        seen = [s["terms"] for ss in sent for s in ss]

        def make(price, **over):
            over = {k: v for k, v in over.items() if k not in pins}
            return satisfy_must_haves(case, {**base, "unit_price": round(price, 2), **over}, std)

        def cost(t):
            return total_cost(case, t, std)

        def cap(t):  # hard floor: never offer a sheet that costs more than the alternative
            if (c := cost(t)) >= c_alt:
                slope = cost({**t, "unit_price": t["unit_price"] + 1}) - c
                if slope > 0:
                    t = {**t, "unit_price": round(t["unit_price"] - (c - c_alt) / slope - 0.01, 2)}
            return t

        def one(price):  # one sheet: for each negotiable lever the option with the lowest C (pinned ones stay theirs)
            over = {}
            for f in FREE_LEVERS if _health_at_stake(case) else LEVERS:
                options = [o for o in opts.get(f, []) if o] if f in case["negotiable"] and f not in pins else []
                if options:
                    over[f] = min(options, key=lambda o: cost(make(price, **over, **{f: o})))
            return cap(make(price, **over))

        price = self._price(case, events, p)
        main = one(price)
        floor = max((x["terms"]["unit_price"] for ss in sent for x in ss[:1] if x["terms"].get("unit_price")), default=0.0)
        while (main in seen or main["unit_price"] <= floor) and price < p:  # always a visible step, never a repeat, never above theirs
            price = min(p, price + _tick(p))
            new = one(price)
            if new == main:  # capped: the price cannot move
                break
            main = new
        if self._stalled(case, events, std):  # close the gap to <= GAP of their C, never past c_open
            f = lambda x: cost(one(x))
            target, lo, hi = (1 - GAP) * cost(theirs), main["unit_price"], p
            if f(hi) >= target:  # smallest price that reaches the target
                for _ in range(30):
                    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                    lo, hi = (lo, mid) if f(mid) >= target else (mid, hi)
            if f(hi) > self._c_open:  # largest price that stays within c_open
                lo = main["unit_price"]
                for _ in range(30):
                    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                    lo, hi = (mid, hi) if f(mid) <= self._c_open else (lo, mid)
                hi = lo
            hi = round(hi, 2)
            while hi > main["unit_price"] and f(hi) > self._c_open:  # rounding must not pass c_open
                hi = round(hi - 0.01, 2)
            if hi > main["unit_price"]:
                main = one(hi)
        if main in seen:
            return []
        out, variants = [main], []
        # the index clause is security for them, not cash: offer it at the price where our C stays just below main's
        for clause in (c for c in opts.get("index_clause", []) if c) if "index_clause" in case["negotiable"] and "index_clause" not in pins else []:
            t = make(main["unit_price"], index_clause=clause, **{f: main[f] for f in LEVERS if f in main})
            slope = cost({**t, "unit_price": t["unit_price"] + 1}) - cost(t)
            if t["index_clause"] == clause != main.get("index_clause") and slope > 0:
                price = round(max(0.75 * p, min(p, t["unit_price"] - (cost(t) - cost(main)) / slope - 0.01)), 2)  # no lowball
                v = cap({**t, "unit_price": price})
                if v not in seen and cost(v) < cost(main):
                    variants.append(v)
        if variants:
            out.append(max(variants, key=lambda v: v["unit_price"]))
        return [complete_offer(case, t) for t in out]
# Plan: a varied mock of the arena (no credits used)

Goal: test our players on many different cases, so they cannot memorise the 10 hosted practice cases and still do well on the hidden final cases. Status: **plan only, nothing built yet.**

## What is verified (sources: `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/api.md`, the data package, our `arena_kit/sim.py`)

- `GET /v1/cases?set=practice` returns every practice case file in full, including the `buyer` block (need, fallback price, interest rate, goal, must-haves, alternative). `?set=sandbox` returns D01 and D02. These calls open no session and use none of the 200 practice sessions. Only `POST /v1/sessions` counts.
- Sandbox sessions (D01, D02) do not count against the quota and have no leaderboard.
- Each case lists `refs` and `facts` that point into the data package, so cases can be tied to real rows.
- Data package (`negotiation-arena-kit/data/`, 8.2 MB, fictional company Hollerau Pumpenwerke, real public market indices): 447 suppliers (46 detailed), 60 parts, 108 quotes in 47 RFQs, 300 past price events (`negotiation_history`: asked % vs settled %), 414 scorecards, 46 contracts, 208 letters/notes, index series.
- Our local simulator (`agent/arena_kit/sim.py`, `sim_cases/S01-S03`) speaks the real API but its supplier is one fixed script (opens 10% above, concedes 2% per sheet to 90%, price-only final offer from round 5). The scoring code in `arena_kit/cost.py` is the arena's own.

## What cannot be recovered

- The real suppliers' hidden floors and exact behaviour. Replays hide their figures (shown as an ellipsis).
- The hidden final cases and the Sunday 08:00 data release.
- So mock results only partly predict the final. Treat them as a robustness test, not a score forecast.

## Steps

1. **Fetch** the practice and sandbox case files (read-only, 0 sessions) and save them under `agent/arena_kit/sim_cases/real/`. Never commit the API key.
2. **Compare** each case's fields and refs with the data package; note which buyer fields are not in the data (fallback price, rates, goal), because those must be copied or varied from real case files, never invented.
3. **Generator:** build new cases from real supplier/part pairs in the data. Vary need, fallback price, rates, goal, must-haves, alternative, quote values and case type (price_increase, renewal, rfq, bundling, raw_material, capacity, quality). The existing scoring recomputes `c_open` and `c_best`.
4. **Supplier model:** replace the fixed script with parameters (opening premium, concession rate, floor, final-offer round), with ranges taken from `negotiation_history` (asked vs settled) and from the replays. Randomise per seed.
5. **Split** the generated cases into a development set (tune on it) and a held-out test set (each agent scored on it once, never tuned on).
6. **Evaluate** all eight players (`Players/Originals/`) over many seeds; rank by the mean across seeds and by the worst case, not by one case.
7. **Guard against hard-coding:** agents must read case fields, never case IDs; a test greps the agents for case-ID strings.
8. Log results in `backlog.csv` (version format `v<N> - <name>`).

## Optional real-API use (needs the owner's approval each time)

- Sandbox runs (D01, D02): free, suggested 5-10 to see real supplier reactions.
- Practice replays: suggested 20 sessions in total (10 with the naive agent, one per hosted case; 10 with Patient Hawk). Gain is steep for the first 10, smaller for the next 10, and flat after that, because only 10 cases are hosted. Not verified: whether suppliers are random; if a rerun differs, extra runs only measure that noise.
- 3 of 200 sessions are used so far (real practice P01, P03, P07). The quota resets on a rolling 24 h.

## Workflow

Follow `CLAUDE.md`: plan first, `coder` writes code, `reviewer` checks every change, tests in `agent/tests/`.

company's data, negotiates **by e-mail** against supplier bots, and **accepts one supplier term sheet or walks

## 4. How a negotiation works

- A **case** = one negotiation (trigger such as a price-increase letter, expiring contract or RFQ + case file + 1-3 supplier bots).
- Round 0: suppliers send a quote e-mail with a quote PDF.
- Your message: subject, body, **up to 3 term sheets** (only term sheets bind), data IDs you rely on, optional text attachments.
- Supplier replies with a status: `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (you still have to accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In RFQ cases 2-3 suppliers run in parallel; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** 10 messages per thread (default), **60 s per message** from the supplier's reply. Late = your last offer repeated and supplier patience drops; 3 in a row ends the thread. Supplier replies can take up to ~1 min (not counted against you).
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** in its quote PDF. Read the PDF before accepting.
- Supplier behaviour: never sells below cost floor; bigger moves need boss approval; cited data is checked by ID; reacts to tone and what you signal; "padding does not buy price". Suppliers differ (family foundry, group with approval ladder, cash-short job shop, near-monopolist).

## 5. Scoring

- Only the accepted term sheet scores: **total cost C** of covering a fixed need over a fixed horizon (price, uncovered need at fallback price + risk, payment-term interest, freight, lead time, quality/PPM, index clause, and supplier-health margin for `stabilise`/`secure_supply` goals).
- **Case score = (C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)**, clipped to 0..1. `C_open` = best opening quote; `C_best` = best package any supplier would ever accept (hidden) or your alternative.
- No deal scores your alternative (0 if none). **A broken must-have scores 0.** Some cases are best left without a deal.
- Final: each wave 0-100 (mean case score x 100); up to **500 points** over 5 waves.
- Category goals: `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`.
- Use `arena_kit.total_cost` to compute C for every term sheet. Formula is in `api.md`.
- Worked example in the brief: asking EUR 43.20/30 days, deal EUR 41.60/60 days, best 40.80/90 days gives score 0.64. A 12-month deal that covers half the need can score 0.

## 6. Data (what the agent mines)

"""SimplifyAgent: slim reciprocal agent. Anchor, steady matched concessions, RFQ round-robin.

Every choice among candidate sheets is priced with cost.total_cost, over the five parts of C:
1. price: anchor 0.80 x theirs, steady concessions matched to theirs;
2. uncovered need: contract length and volume are the options with the lowest C (never leave need uncovered);
3. payment, freight, lead time: each negotiable lever takes its lowest-C option, unless the supplier pinned it;
4. quality and other: ppm commitment likewise, plus a second sheet with an index clause for a higher price;
5. the supplier's health (strategic / bottleneck goals with a relationship cost): C charges for leaving the supplier below a
   sustainable margin, but the buyer cannot estimate its full cost (should-cost exists for about half the parts and can exceed
   the price), so cost.total_cost sees 0 and the mock does not price it. Safer rule there, UNTESTED against the real penalty:
   anchor 0.90 and only levers that cost the supplier nothing (contract length, volume); payment, freight, lead time and
   quality stay at the supplier's own terms.

Closing, must-have and pin helpers are shared with reciprocal.py."""

import math

from ..cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, complete_offer, total_cost
from ..docs import standard_terms
from ..guard import satisfy_must_haves
from ..play import closing_move, latest, moves_left
from .reciprocal import (
    ANCHOR,
    ANCHOR_FLOOR,
    FRAC0,
    FRAC_MAX,
    FRAC_STEP,
    KEEP,
    MATCH,
    MIN_STEP,
    MOVING_MIN,
    _c_alt,
    _live,
    _mine,
    _pinned,
    _sup,
    _tick,
    _valid,
    case_c_open,
    closing_accept,
)

EASED_ANCHOR = 0.90
STALL = 0.01  # the supplier's best C fell by less than this (x C) across its last two replies: it has stalled
GAP = 0.05  # then our offer rises until it is at most this far (x their C) below theirs
FREE_LEVERS = ("contract_months", "volume_per_year")  # cost the supplier nothing in cash
LEVERS = ("contract_months", "volume_per_year", "payment_days", "incoterm", "lead_time_days", "ppm_commitment")


def _health_at_stake(case):
    """C charges for the supplier's margin (strategic / bottleneck goal with a price per margin point)."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    return b.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS and bool(b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"))


class SimplifyAgent:
    _c_open = math.inf  # set per decision; our offer never costs more than the closing rule would accept

    def decide(self, case, threads):
        if not _live(threads):  # nothing to answer
            return {"supplier_id": next(iter(threads), None), "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        if accept := closing_accept(case, threads):
            return accept
        live = [s for s in _live(threads) if moves_left(case, threads[s]) >= 1]
        open_ = [s for s in live if latest(threads[s]).get("status") not in ("final_offer", "agreed")]
        if not open_:
            return closing_move(case, threads)

        def key(s):  # keep every thread moving: fewest messages first, then the cheapest
            ev = threads[s]
            c = min((c for c, _ in _valid(case, ev, standard_terms(ev), math.inf, musts=False)), default=math.inf)
            return len(_mine(ev)), c

        sid = min(open_, key=key)
        # cap: the opening and the best standing sheet of any other open thread
        others = [c for s in open_ if s != sid for c, _ in _valid(case, threads[s], standard_terms(threads[s]), math.inf)]
        self._c_open = min([case_c_open(case, threads), *others])
        events = threads[sid]
        std = standard_terms(events)
        valid = _valid(case, events, std, math.inf) or _valid(case, events, std, math.inf, musts=False)  # a must-have breach is fixed in our sheet
        if not valid:  # no priced sheet to answer: ask for one, give up after 3 asks
            if len(_mine(events)) >= 3:
                return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
            return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"subject": case.get("title", "Our enquiry"), "body": "Could you please send us your quote?"}}
        _, best = min(valid, key=lambda v: v[0])
        sheets = self._sheets(case, events, std, best["terms"])
        if not sheets:  # nothing new left to offer: close on the best sheet, or give up
            return closing_move(case, threads)
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case.get("title", "Our proposal"),
                "body": "Thank you for your offer. We have moved on our side; please see our updated terms.",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
            },
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _their_move(events):
        """How far the supplier's best price fell in its last message (0 if it did not)."""
        ps = [min(s["terms"]["unit_price"] for s in m["term_sheets"] if s["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None)
              for m in _sup(events) if any(s["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None for s in m["term_sheets"])]
        return max(0.0, ps[-2] - ps[-1]) if len(ps) >= 2 else 0.0

    @staticmethod
    def _stalled(case, events, std):
        """We have opened and the supplier's best C fell by < STALL across its last two replies (3+ priced messages)."""
        cs = [min(total_cost(case, t["terms"], std) for t in m["term_sheets"] if t["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None)
              for m in _sup(events) if any(t["terms"].get("unit_price") is not None for t in m["term_sheets"])]
        return bool(_mine(events)) and len(cs) >= 3 and cs[-3] - cs[-1] < STALL * cs[-3]

    def _price(self, case, events, p):
        mine = [m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"] for m in _mine(events) if m.get("term_sheets") and m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"].get("unit_price")]
        if not mine:
            cur = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price") or p
            return max(ANCHOR_FLOOR * p, min((EASED_ANCHOR if _health_at_stake(case) else ANCHOR) * p, cur))  # anchor; never pay more than now unless forced
        frac = min(FRAC_MAX, FRAC0 + FRAC_STEP * len(mine))
        move = self._their_move(events)
        step = max(frac * (p - mine[-1]), MIN_STEP * p, _tick(p))
        if move > 0:  # they moved: answer in step, not beyond (a supplier that holds still gets the full step)
            step = max(MOVING_MIN * p, _tick(p), min(step, MATCH * move))
        top = p if moves_left(case, events) <= 2 else p * (1 - KEEP)
        return max(mine[-1], min(top, mine[-1] + step))

    def _sheets(self, case, events, std, theirs):
        p, pins = theirs["unit_price"], _pinned(events)
        base = {k: v for k, v in {**{f: std[f] for f in case["negotiable"] if f in std}, **theirs}.items() if v is not None}
        opts = case.get("term_options") or {}
        c_alt = _c_alt(case)
        sent = [m["term_sheets"] for m in _mine(events) if m.get("term_sheets")]
        seen = [s["terms"] for ss in sent for s in ss]

        def make(price, **over):
            over = {k: v for k, v in over.items() if k not in pins}
            return satisfy_must_haves(case, {**base, "unit_price": round(price, 2), **over}, std)

        def cost(t):
            return total_cost(case, t, std)

        def cap(t):  # hard floor: never offer a sheet that costs more than the alternative
            if (c := cost(t)) >= c_alt:
                slope = cost({**t, "unit_price": t["unit_price"] + 1}) - c
                if slope > 0:
                    t = {**t, "unit_price": round(t["unit_price"] - (c - c_alt) / slope - 0.01, 2)}
            return t

        def one(price):  # one sheet: for each negotiable lever the option with the lowest C (pinned ones stay theirs)
            over = {}
            for f in FREE_LEVERS if _health_at_stake(case) else LEVERS:
                options = [o for o in opts.get(f, []) if o] if f in case["negotiable"] and f not in pins else []
                if options:
                    over[f] = min(options, key=lambda o: cost(make(price, **over, **{f: o})))
            return cap(make(price, **over))

        price = self._price(case, events, p)
        main = one(price)
        floor = max((x["terms"]["unit_price"] for ss in sent for x in ss[:1] if x["terms"].get("unit_price")), default=0.0)
        while (main in seen or main["unit_price"] <= floor) and price < p:  # always a visible step, never a repeat, never above theirs
            price = min(p, price + _tick(p))
            new = one(price)
            if new == main:  # capped: the price cannot move
                break
            main = new
        if self._stalled(case, events, std):  # close the gap to <= GAP of their C, never past c_open
            f = lambda x: cost(one(x))
            target, lo, hi = (1 - GAP) * cost(theirs), main["unit_price"], p
            if f(hi) >= target:  # smallest price that reaches the target
                for _ in range(30):
                    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                    lo, hi = (lo, mid) if f(mid) >= target else (mid, hi)
            if f(hi) > self._c_open:  # largest price that stays within c_open
                lo = main["unit_price"]
                for _ in range(30):
                    mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                    lo, hi = (mid, hi) if f(mid) <= self._c_open else (lo, mid)
                hi = lo
            hi = round(hi, 2)
            while hi > main["unit_price"] and f(hi) > self._c_open:  # rounding must not pass c_open
                hi = round(hi - 0.01, 2)
            if hi > main["unit_price"]:
                main = one(hi)
        if main in seen:
            return []
        out, variants = [main], []
        # the index clause is security for them, not cash: offer it at the price where our C stays just below main's
        for clause in (c for c in opts.get("index_clause", []) if c) if "index_clause" in case["negotiable"] and "index_clause" not in pins else []:
            t = make(main["unit_price"], index_clause=clause, **{f: main[f] for f in LEVERS if f in main})
            slope = cost({**t, "unit_price": t["unit_price"] + 1}) - cost(t)
            if t["index_clause"] == clause != main.get("index_clause") and slope > 0:
                price = round(max(0.75 * p, min(p, t["unit_price"] - (cost(t) - cost(main)) / slope - 0.01)), 2)  # no lowball
                v = cap({**t, "unit_price": price})
                if v not in seen and cost(v) < cost(main):
                    variants.append(v)
        if variants:
            out.append(max(variants, key=lambda v: v["unit_price"]))
        return [complete_offer(case, t) for t in out]

- The real suppliers' hidden floors and exact behaviour. Replays hide their figures (shown as an ellipsis).
- The hidden final cases and the Sunday 08:00 data release.
- So mock results only partly predict the final. Treat them as a robustness test, not a score forecast.

## Steps

1. **Fetch** the practice and sandbox case files (read-only, 0 sessions) and save them under `agent/arena_kit/sim_cases/real/`. Never commit the API key.
2. **Compare** each case's fields and refs with the data package; note which buyer fields are not in the data (fallback price, rates, goal), because those must be copied or varied from real case files, never invented.
3. **Generator:** build new cases from real supplier/part pairs in the data. Vary need, fallback price, rates, goal, must-haves, alternative, quote values and case type (price_increase, renewal, rfq, bundling, raw_material, capacity, quality). The existing scoring recomputes `c_open` and `c_best`.
4. **Supplier model:** replace the fixed script with parameters (opening premium, concession rate, floor, final-offer round), with ranges taken from `negotiation_history` (asked vs settled) and from the replays. Randomise per seed.
5. **Split** the generated cases into a development set (tune on it) and a held-out test set (each agent scored on it once, never tuned on).
6. **Evaluate** all eight players (`Players/Originals/`) over many seeds; rank by the mean across seeds and by the worst case, not by one case.
7. **Guard against hard-coding:** agents must read case fields, never case IDs; a test greps the agents for case-ID strings.
8. Log results in `backlog.csv` (version format `v<N> - <name>`).

## Optional real-API use (needs the owner's approval each time)

- Sandbox runs (D01, D02): free, suggested 5-10 to see real supplier reactions.
- Practice replays: suggested 20 sessions in total (10 with the naive agent, one per hosted case; 10 with Patient Hawk). Gain is steep for the first 10, smaller for the next 10, and flat after that, because only 10 cases are hosted. Not verified: whether suppliers are random; if a rerun differs, extra runs only measure that noise.
- 3 of 200 sessions are used so far (real practice P01, P03, P07). The quota resets on a rolling 24 h.

## Workflow

Follow `CLAUDE.md`: plan first, `coder` writes code, `reviewer` checks every change, tests in `agent/tests/`.
# Challenge: Tacto Negotiation Arena

Single source of truth for the challenge. Compiled 2026-10-10 from the official kit
(<https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit>: `brief/brief.md`, `brief/submission.md`,
`starter-kit/README.md`, `data/README.md`) and the organiser's Discord post.
**Not yet read:** `brief/api.md` (full API) and the contents of `data/`. Check the originals before relying on any detail here.

## Sources

| Tag | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| [A] | <https://arena.tacto.ai/> | Overview, one rule, weekend schedule |
| [K] | <https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit> | Brief, rules, scoring, data, starter kit, submission (sections 1-11) |
| [P] | <https://arena.tacto.ai/apply> | Key flow: match code, key shown once, `.env`, keep out of git (section 3) |
| [L] | <https://arena.tacto.ai/live> | Practice board, house-agent scores, team standings (section 14) |
| [F] | <https://arena.tacto.ai/faq> | Scoring FAQ, deployment, token costs, P01 replay (section 14) |

Sections 1-11 come mainly from [K] with [A] and [P]; section 14 comes from [L] and [F]. The Discord post is the organiser's announcement.

> **Status: candidate project, not yet chosen.** Never put the arena key, `.env` or any LLM key in this repo (the repo is public).

## 1. The task in one paragraph

Build an **AI buyer agent** for a fictional German pump maker (Hollerau Pumpenwerke, ~45 suppliers). It reads the
company's data, negotiates **by e-mail** against supplier bots, and **accepts one supplier term sheet or walks
away**. Score = **total cost in EUR**, not unit price. Practice all weekend; the **Live Final** (Sun 12:00) runs
on hidden cases against unseen suppliers. Bring your own LLM; Tacto runs the suppliers.

## 2. Key dates and links

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive, ground floor. **Challenge selection closes 13:00.** |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; Discord until 23:00 |
| Sun 08:00 | **Second data release.** Run `uv run arena data` again; hidden cases may cite it |
| Sun 09:00 | Pre-flight: one practice case through the final setup |
| Sun 11:30 | Checklist (section 8) |
| **Sun 12:00** | **Code freeze + Live Final** (5 waves x 8 min, all teams at once). Submit on **ehl.gg** |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch: 5 min + 2 min questions |
| Sun 14:30 / 15:30 / 16:30 | Winners announced / Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) / Awards |

Links: [arena](https://arena.tacto.ai) · [apply for key](https://arena.tacto.ai/apply) · [practice board](https://arena.tacto.ai/live) · [results](https://arena.tacto.ai/results) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) · [kit repo](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)

**Prizes:** 1st place EUR 1,500, medals for top 3, best 2 EHL finalist teams go to the Grand Final.
How the Live Final score and jury score combine is **still undecided** (placeholder in the brief, "decided Sat morning"). Ask on Discord.

## 3. Getting the key (one per team)

1. Apply at `arena.tacto.ai/apply` (team name + contact e-mail; a name starting with one emoji shows on the big screen).
2. Show the match code at the Tacto desk.
3. Copy the key. **It is shown once.** Lost it: organisers reset it at the desk.
4. Put it in `.env` as `ARENA_API_KEY=...`. Never post or commit it.

Only **one person** should hold the team key. Share it privately, not in git, chat threads or Discord.

## 4. How a negotiation works

- A **case** = one negotiation (trigger such as a price-increase letter, expiring contract or RFQ + case file + 1-3 supplier bots).
- Round 0: suppliers send a quote e-mail with a quote PDF.
- Your message: subject, body, **up to 3 term sheets** (only term sheets bind), data IDs you rely on, optional text attachments.
- Supplier replies with a status: `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (you still have to accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In RFQ cases 2-3 suppliers run in parallel; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** 10 messages per thread (default), **60 s per message** from the supplier's reply. Late = your last offer repeated and supplier patience drops; 3 in a row ends the thread. Supplier replies can take up to ~1 min (not counted against you).
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** in its quote PDF. Read the PDF before accepting.
- Supplier behaviour: never sells below cost floor; bigger moves need boss approval; cited data is checked by ID; reacts to tone and what you signal; "padding does not buy price". Suppliers differ (family foundry, group with approval ladder, cash-short job shop, near-monopolist).

## 5. Scoring

- Only the accepted term sheet scores: **total cost C** of covering a fixed need over a fixed horizon (price, uncovered need at fallback price + risk, payment-term interest, freight, lead time, quality/PPM, index clause, and supplier-health margin for `stabilise`/`secure_supply` goals).
- **Case score = (C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)**, clipped to 0..1. `C_open` = best opening quote; `C_best` = best package any supplier would ever accept (hidden) or your alternative.
- No deal scores your alternative (0 if none). **A broken must-have scores 0.** Some cases are best left without a deal.
- Final: each wave 0-100 (mean case score x 100); up to **500 points** over 5 waves.
- Category goals: `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine`.
- Use `arena_kit.total_cost` to compute C for every term sheet. Formula is in `api.md`.
- Worked example in the brief: asking EUR 43.20/30 days, deal EUR 41.60/60 days, best 40.80/90 days gives score 0.64. A 12-month deal that covers half the need can score 0.

## 6. Data (what the agent mines)

Data package v1: CSV + `world.sqlite` + `facts.json` + contracts + letters/e-mails/notes. Key tables: suppliers (447),
parts (60), price_conditions, negotiation_history, contracts + clauses, po_lines, goods_receipts, invoices,
quality_notifications, scorecards, forecasts, rfqs/quotes, spend_cube, index_series/index_values (real public
market series), cost_drivers, should_cost, news, documents. Company "today" is **2026-09-30**.

- Every citable fact has an ID: `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`.
- Reply marks each cited claim `verified`, `contradicted` (wrong figure/unknown ID, **costs trust**), `irrelevant` or `duplicate`.
- **True data is not automatically rewarded.** Read the supplier's situation (notes, letters, news, quote remarks) and find the trade it wants (a cash-short supplier may value payment days more than price).
- Some notes are noise. Sunday 08:00 release adds news, letters and a memo.
- Download: `uv run arena data` or `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`.

## 7. Rules

- **No human in the loop** during the Live Final. Start the agent before 12:00 and leave it running.
- The agent **must not read** `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` (or their JSON) during the Final. `arena board` is for humans only.
- One API key per team. No attacks on the service or other teams.
- One attempt per case in the final. Everything else counts, including weaknesses found in the bots; replays are open to the jury.
- Max 10 open sessions per key. Client limit ~10 calls/s.
- A supplier remembers only within a case.
- Up to **one third of hidden cases combine supplier/case types practice never shows**. Memorising practice suppliers will not work.

## 8. Practice and tooling

- **Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 h (`uv run arena me` shows usage). Plan runs.
- Needs Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
cp .env.example .env              # add ARENA_API_KEY (and the LLM provider settings)
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena me                   # team + quota
uv run arena play case:P01 -v     # naive agent, one practice case; prints score + replay link
uv run arena data                 # download data (rerun Sun 08:00)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8
uv run arena board                # practice leaderboard (humans only)
```

- **No key yet:** `arena-sim` runs the API locally (one plain scripted supplier; teaches the API contract, not real supplier behaviour).
- **LLM:** `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or `openai` for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Must answer within 60 s: use a fast model, do heavy research before opening a session. Tacto says a small cheap model is enough; reading the data matters more.
- **MCP server over the data:** `uv run arena mcp --data <path>` (6 read-only tools) lets Claude Code query the data.
- Own agent = any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": ..., "message": {...}}`. Kit helpers: `total_cost`, `complete_offer`, `standard_terms`, `play`, `play_waves`.
- Kit's final runner: `uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10`. It waits for each wave, closes cases 90 s before the cap, and resumes after a crash.

## 9. Submission (ehl.gg, by Sun 12:00)

1. **Repo** with the agent and a README to run it (setup, env var names without values, command). Include the **commit hash** run in the final. Jury and tum.ai (runs a code agent over submissions) must be able to open it. **No keys in the repo.**
2. **Short description:** how the agent prepares, what it reads, how it decides offers, when it closes or walks.
3. **Slides** for the pitch (top 10 only present).
4. Do not push after the freeze; the top 10 are checked for it.

**Checklist for 11:30:** final machine and network tested at the 09:00 pre-flight; `arena data` rerun after 08:00; `arena me` works; LLM credits and rate limits for ~1 h of parallel play; runner started and logging to a file; laptop on power, sleep disabled.

## 10. Pitch

5 min + 2 min questions. Walk the jury through one replay. Expected questions: Why did your agent write that? Would it work on a real supplier? What did it learn about suppliers, and from where? Draft jury criteria: approach, explainability, craft (not final).

## 11. Strategy notes (from the brief's tips)

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; LLM picks arguments and wording.
- Read the supplier before arguing; read the quote PDF before accepting.
- Send 2-3 term sheets to learn what a supplier values; ask the roles (engineering, finance, quality) the right questions.
- Don't leak urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- The kit's LLM agent is a **starting point, not a winner**. It only sees what the case file points to.
- Refuse bad accepts; fall back to a safe move if the model times out.
- Consider building our own supplier simulator from the public data to test against.
- Rehearse the final: all hosted cases in parallel from the final machine, well inside 8 minutes.

## 12. Open questions / risks

- How final score and jury score combine for places 1-3 (undecided in the brief).
- `api.md` not yet read here; `data/` contents not yet explored.
- Wave themes are revealed on the day. The host may extend a wave cap.
- Practice quota (200/24 h) limits brute-force tuning.
- Key handling in a public repo: use `.env` (listed in the root `.gitignore`) and a secrets check before every push.

## 13. Suggested team split (maps to our subagents)

| Role | Owner | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Manager | main session / team lead | plan, assign, track the freeze deadline |
| `coder` | build agent | strategy module, cost pricing, term-sheet logic |
| `reviewer` | check agent | review diffs, hunt key leaks and unsafe accepts |
| `teacher` | explain | explain data and code to teammates |
| Data analyst (human) | mine the data | which index/clause/note moves which supplier |
| Pitch (human) | slides and replay walkthrough | |

## 14. From the arena website (arena.tacto.ai, snapshot Sat 10 Oct, build phase)

Pages: `/` overview, `/apply` key flow, `/live` practice board, `/results` final standings (empty until wave 1), `/faq`.

**Practice board (22 teams, 12 active in the last hour at snapshot).** Best team mean was 0.68; most teams had met 1 of 10 suppliers. Nobody had beaten Tacto's **house agent** on any of the 10 bots.

| Case | Type | Supplier | House agent | Best team |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | Price increase | Brandlhuber (family foundry, +9.5% volute casings) | 0.97 | 0.93 |
| P02 | Price increase | Nordmark (copper pass-through, 7.5 kW motor) | 0.74 | none |
| P03 | Renewal | Selvbrunn Drive Systems (frequency converter) | 0.92 | 0.90 |
| P04 | Renewal | Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd (ball bearing 6306) | 0.86 | none |
| P05 | RFQ (3 bidders) | Dralveck / Hrvelec / Fuchsreiter (pump shaft) | 0.56 | 0.36 |
| P07 | Bundling | Schraubenhandel Leitner (fastener kit) | 0.78 | 0.74 |
| P08 | Raw material | Edelstahl-Service Donautal (1.4404 bar) | 0.75 | none |
| P10 | Capacity | Ravensteiner (seal allocation cut) | 0.69 | 0.45 |
| P11 | Quality | Kalwisz (bearing brackets in red) | 0.31 | none |
| P18 | Raw material | Blankstahl Werdenfels (1.4404 bar) | 0.39 | none |

Takeaways: the house agent scores 0.31-0.97, so quality and capacity cases (P11, P18, P10) are hardest. Beating the house agent is a visible goal. Sandbox cases `case:D01`, `case:D02` do **not** count against the 200/day quota.

**FAQ highlights**
- **Ranking is by points, not euros.** Every case weighs the same; "EUR saved" is a side number (mention it in the pitch). Ties: more deals, then fewer rounds.
- **Nothing to deploy.** The agent is an API client; no server or public URL. Real suppliers exist only on arena.tacto.ai. For the final, **a cloud VM is safer than a laptop on venue Wi-Fi.** Tacto does not run our code; we run the submitted commit ourselves.

The same index argument sent as an ultimatum got EUR 136.50 from November: roughly EUR 13,700 a year worse. **Tone and trades beat threats.**
- A deal that covers only part of the need (for example 12 months instead of 24) can score 0 even at a lower unit price.
